CODE FOR BASIC REQUIREMENTS FOR DELIVERY PERSONS ENGAGED IN THE DELIVERY OF LPG CYLINDERS

Gas Cylinders Sectional Committee, HMD 16

FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 8 March 1990, after the draft finalized by the Oas Cylinders Sectional Committee had been approved by the Heavy Mechanical Engineering Division Council Currently, the number of persons engaged in delivery of LPG cylinders to consumers is around 20,000 persons. With the addition of customers at the present level about 500 new persons would be added to this trade every year. At present there are no formal programmes/training schools to train these persons so that they know the minimum safety levels required to ensure safety of the consumers and that of the equipment. Since these numbers are increasing everyday it is considered that with the issue of this standard, a number of aspects of delivery of LPG cylinder to customers would be taken care of by making the persons observe minimum safety levels at all times. This standard will, thus, help increase in the safety levels and also increase the equipment life in the long way.

AMENDMENT NO. 1 APRIL 1998 TO IS 12936 : 1990 CODE FOR BASIC REQUIREMENTS FOR DELIVERY PERSONS ENGAGED IN THE DELIVERY OF LPG CYLINDERS

Indian Standard CODE FOR BASIC REQUIREMENTS FOR DELIVERY PERSONS ENGAGED IN THE DELIVERY OF LPG CYLINDERS
1 SCOPE 1.1 This code limits the responsibility of delivery persons after the receipt of filled cylinders at the godown, checking of net weight of the contents, transportation to customer's premises, disconnecting of the old consumed cyclinder and replacing it with a filled cylinder, testing for leak and/or other difficulties and bringing back the empty cylinders to godown. 4 BASIC REQUIREMENTS 4.1 Age All persons engaged in delivery of cylinders to customers shall have attained the age of adulthood, that is, 18 years. 4.2 Educational Qualification

IS 12936 : 1990 ii) Purpose of breather-hole/gencral defects in pressure regulator etc. c) Rubber Tubing Standard rubber tubing/condition of rubber tubing when to be changed/probable places where rubber tube wears out fast. d) LPG Stove Familiarity with various cooking appliances for use with LPG. e) Cylinder Valves i) 'O' Ring/joint packing and its importance. ii) Various types of leakage through valves and their precautionery measures, etc. f) Detection of gas leakages (water or soap not to be used for valve pin leakage). g) Precautions to be taken while transporting LPG cylinders, from godowns to customer premises. h) Precautions to be taken at the customers' premises. j) Educating customers on simple Do's and Don'ts. k) Handling emergencies -- Knowledge of Do's and Dont's in the event of leakages. m) Safety rules of LPG and statutory rules regarding handling, transportation and storage of LPG cylinders. n) Visual identification for detection of spurious cylinders, valves and regulators.
NOTE -- The above are the general guidelines to be covered while training the delivery persons. Based on the technology of the equipment if any other material is required to be communicated to the delivery person, the same may also be included.

Standard Mark

The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.
